newsitem.title: UK: GCC must look beyond oil to capital markets - banker.
newsitem.headline: GCC must look beyond oil to capital markets - banker.

text.p: Middle East Gulf oil producers should lessen their dependency on oil revenue and encourage foreign investment but must first introduce reforms, a senior Middle East banker said on Tuesday.

Sharif Ghalib, senior vice president and chief economist at the Gulf Investment Corporation based in Kuwait, told the Oil and Money conference that the prospect of flat oil prices over the next several years made these reforms especially necessary.
"It is still this heavy dependence on hydrocarbon revenues that poses challenges -- economic, financial and sociopolitical -- for the GCC," he said.
Ghalib said the six members of the Gulf Cooperation Council used hydrocarbon revenues to pay for more than 75 percent of their budgets.
He said the biggest challenge facing the GCC in its move to diversify its economies was to make better use of capital markets
"The GCC needs to improve the depth, liqidity and use of capital markets in the region to influence direct foreign investment," he said.
Ghalib said the GCC should also make better use of project financing through lease schemes and to step-up its nascent privatisation.
He said Kuwait has been especially successful in its privatisation campaign, raising $1.3 billion since mid 1994.
"Through faster forms and the use of several fiancing instruments companies should not write off the GCC as a place to do business," he told the conference.
